item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Nov. 8)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Trump says U.S. took a "giant step back in history" with midterm results
item.description: President Trump on Sunday said the U.S. "took a giant step back in history" as his White House continued to roil from his post-midterm shakeup

item.title: Nature: Fall colors in Texas
item.description: We leave you this Sunday in the peace and quiet of the Lost Maples State Natural Area in Vanderpool, Texas. Videographer: Scot Miller.

item.title: Photos of the week
item.description: "Sunday Morning" looks at some of the most evocative images captured the week of Nov. 1-7, 2026.

item.title: With "Thrasher," Brandon Flowers returns home
item.description: Smalltown Nephi, Utah, was where the musical sensibilities of Killers frontman Brandon Flowers started to take form, before finding success as a rock star in Las Vegas. Now his solo album, "Thrasher," is filled with country songs like those beloved by his dad.

item.title: Iran downplays new U.S. task force aimed at disrupting land routes
item.description: The U.S. did not say whether any military action would be involved in preventing weapons technology or sanctioned items from entering Iran.

item.title: Jon Meacham on the midterms and America's "better angels"
item.description: In last week's historic elections, voters were asked to weigh in on whether our nation will maintain the ideals of equality, dignity, fair play, and the rule of law; historian Jon Meacham says that Americans overwhelmingly answered, and democracy prevailed.

item.title: Jon Meacham on the midterms and America's "better angels"
item.description: Reflecting on this week's historic midterm elections, in which voters were asked to weigh in on whether our nation will maintain the ideals of equality, dignity, fair play, and the rule of law, historian Jon Meacham says that Americans overwhelmingly answered – and that democracy has prevailed.

item.title: Judi Dench on an actor's life
item.description: A film producer once told Judi Dench she had "everything wrong with her face." One Oscar and a Damehood later, she's had the last laugh. The actress, now 91, talks about her new memoir, "Is It Too Late to Make a Run for It?"

item.title: Extended interview: Dame Judi Dench and Brendan O'Hea
item.description: In this web exclusive, Dame Judi Dench discusses her new memoir, "Is It Too Late to Make a Run for It?," co-written with friend and fellow actor Brendan O'Hea. She also talks with Seth Doane about Shakespeare, James Bond, her vision loss, playing practical jokes, and never taking her success for granted.

item.title: Judi Dench on an actor's life
item.description: A film producer once told Judi Dench she had "everything wrong with her face." Eight Academy Award nominations, one Oscar, and a Damehood later, she's had the last laugh. The actress, now 91, talks with correspondent Seth Doane about her extraordinary career, losing much of her eyesight, and her new memoir, "Is It Too Late to Make a Run for It?," co-written with friend and fellow actor Brendan O'Hea.

item.title: Love at long last: "It was just a fluke"
item.description: In Bay City, Michigan, 65-year-old Al Sager and 76-year-old Susan Guc were both content with being single their whole lives – committed to being uncommitted – until they both underwent heart procedures and were placed in the same cardiac rehab program. Steve Hartman reports on how true love took the long way 'round, proving that it's never too late to find love.

item.title: Poland mourns Krakow shooting victims as terrorism probe launched
item.description: The attack, which Poland's defense minister described as an "act of terror," happened in Main Square, a major tourist hub in the heart of Krakow's Old Town.

item.title: Rick Lowe: Turning data and social research into art
item.description: In his latest exhibition, at the University of Michigan Museum of Art in Ann Arbor, artist Rick Lowe explores a complex, untold story of Black America, by translating socio-economic data about progress made by Black Americans into art. Correspondent Martha Teichner talks with Lowe about his own life's upward trajectory.

item.title: Passage: In memoriam
item.description: "Sunday Morning" remembers some of the notable figures who left us this week, including actress Elke Sommer, who starred in the Pink Panther caper "A Shot in the Dark."

item.title: "The Altruists" actor Julia Garner on surprising herself
item.description: In "The Altruists," the Emmy-winning star of "Ozark" plays Caroline Ellison, girlfriend of Sam Bankman-Fried and business partner in a multi-billion-dollar cryptocurrency fraud. Jennifer Garner talks about how, for her, the eyes truly are the windows to the soul.

item.title: Extended interview: Julia Garner
item.description: In this web exclusive, Emmy-winner Julia Garner ("Ozark," "Inventing Anna") talks with correspondent Anthony Mason about her new Netflix series, "The Altruists." She also discusses her childhood, her brain (which she describes as "odd"), and dissecting a performance.

item.title: "The Altruists" actor Julia Garner on surprising herself
item.description: In the new Netflix series "The Altruists," three-time Emmy Award-winner Julia Garner ("Ozark," "Inventing Anna") stars as Caroline Ellison, girlfriend of Sam Bankman-Fried and business partner in a multi-billion-dollar cryptocurrency fraud. Garner talks with correspondent Anthony Mason about being hired to play "the most unhinged people," and why watching a movie can give her an "endless sense of hope."

item.title: The SS United States and her final destination
item.description: She was the fastest ocean liner in history. But the jet age took the SS United States out of service, and she wound up docked in Philadelphia for nearly 30 years. Now, she's scheduled to be scuttled off Florida, to become the world's largest artificial reef.

item.title: The SS United States and her final destination
item.description: She was the fastest ocean liner in history, widely known as America's flagship, and in her nearly two decades in service, the elegant SS United States carried four presidents, countless celebrities, and tens of thousands of happy voyagers. But the jet age took her out of service, and she eventually wound up docked at a Philadelphia berth for close to 30 years. Now, the SS United States is scheduled to sink off the coast of Florida, to become the world's largest artificial reef. Correspondent Lee Cowan looks back on the history and future of a maritime legend.

item.title: Leading Dem on midterms aftermath: "We're still in the fight of our lives"
item.description: The midterms marked one of the biggest rebukes of the Republican Party since Watergate. What is the fallout from this year's elections, and how are Democrats going to address a lame-duck President Trump?

item.title: Leading Dem on midterms aftermath: "We're still in the fight of our lives"
item.description: Last Tuesday's midterm elections marked one of the biggest rebukes of the Republican Party since Watergate, with Democrats winning control of both houses of Congress. "Sunday Morning" national correspondent Robert Costa talks with Democratic Congressman Jamie Raskin and former Republican Governor Larry Hogan about the fallout from this year's elections, and how Democrats are going to address a lame-duck President Trump.

item.title: Almanac: November 8
item.description: "Sunday Morning" looks back at historical events on this date.

item.title: Seeking relief from chronic pain
item.description: With about one in four American adults living with chronic pain, Dr. Jon LaPook examines some of the current treatments, from medications and surgery, to nerve stimulation, biofeedback and self-hypnosis.

item.title: Seeking relief from chronic pain
item.description: About one in four American adults lives with chronic pain, defined as pain lasting more than three months. Most are still suffering for a year or longer. CBS News chief medical correspondent Dr. Jon LaPook examines some of the current treatments aimed at alleviating chronic pain, from medications and surgery, to nerve stimulation, biofeedback and self-hypnosis.

item.title: Villa Vie Odyssey "forever cruise" residents want their ship back
item.description: Some residents of the Villa Vie Odyssey cruise are trying to reclaim the ship, which could potentially be auctioned off by its lender, CBS News has learned.

item.title: ICE unlikely to scale back crackdown, sources say, citing Stephen Miller
item.description: The Trump administration is unlikely to scale back its aggressive crackdown on illegal immigration following the results of the midterm elections, multiple U.S. officials told CBS News, citing the elevation of Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff.

item.title: OC fishermen find cruise ship employee treading water miles off coast
item.description: Two Newport Beach fishermen found a Royal Caribbean cruise ship employee treading water nearly 20 miles off the coast while returning home from a fishing trip near Catalina Island on Friday.

item.title: NYC schools employee faces murder charge in Brooklyn jogger's killing
item.description: A New York City Department of Education employee is facing a murder charge in the stabbing death of a 28-year-old woman last week in Brooklyn, authorities announced Saturday.

item.title: Book excerpt: "Is It Too Late to Make a Run For It?" by Judi Dench with Brendan O'Hea
item.description: The celebrated actress' latest book – conversations with friend and fellow actor Brendan O'Hea – revisits an extraordinary career and a remarkable life, from Shakespeare to Bond.
